item.title: MJR Morning Brief — October 27, 2026
item.description:
From Media Jobs Report, here's what's happening across the media industry.
FCC Commissioner Anna Gomez is urging broadcasters to resist political intimidation ahead of the midterm elections. In a letter to the National Association of Broadcasters, Gomez warned that airing polling results the Trump administration dislikes does not justify an FCC investigation. She emphasized that broadcasters must protect their editorial independence and should never have to choose between their licenses and their integrity.
In radio news,
Mentoring and Inspiring Women in Radio has selected Callie Luttman, morning host at Saga Communications' Mix 94.5 in Champaign-Urbana, as its 2026 Behind the Mic mentee. The year-long program provides leadership coaching and industry mentorship, along with an opportunity to attend the 2027 NAB Show in Las Vegas.
Turning to podcasts,
The ninth annual Canadian Podcast Awards are accepting nominations through November fourteenth. Canadian podcast professionals can nominate eligible shows across thirty-one categories, with winners selected by industry members. Public voting is also available through the People's Choice category. Winners will be announced December sixteenth.
In music news,
Warner Music Group is combining its recorded music and publishing synchronization operations into one global division, promoting industry veteran Ron Broitman to President of Global Sync. The restructuring will simplify music licensing, speed up approvals and expand opportunities for artists and songwriters. Broitman will oversee worldwide sync operations across Warner's labels and publishing divisions.
Turning to radio,
Benztown is spreading holiday cheer with its free Christmas AudioPack, featuring 50 festive audio elements for radio stations of every format. From holiday sound effects to seasonal production elements, it's everything stations need to get into the Christmas spirit. Get the free pack at Benztown dot com slash Christmas.
In music news,
Warner Music Group has promoted Roberto Andrade Dirak to President of Warner Music Latina and A&R for Latin America. Based in Miami, Andrade will expand his oversight of artist development, signings, and regional strategy. He has led Warner Music Latina for five years, helping develop rising Latin talent and strengthen the label's international presence.
Turning to television,
Telemundo Las Vegas has added two journalists to its news team. Samanta Rodríguez joins as meteorologist after more than five years at Telemundo 39 in Dallas-Fort Worth. Ana Sofía Román joins as multimedia journalist from CoastTV News and Telemundo Delmarva. The 2026 Capital Emmy winner brings experience covering immigration, housing and local government. Both debuted October 26 on Noticiero Telemundo Las Vegas.
In awards and recognition news,
Audacy picked up five honors at the 2026 Buffalo Broadcasters Awards. WGR Sports Radio 550 was named Station of the Year, while WBEN's "A New Morning" won Radio Program of the Year. Sal Capaccio earned Sports Professional of the Year, his "It's Always Gameday in Buffalo" podcast won Podcast of the Year, and Owen Parker was named Breakout Talent of the Year.
And finally,
TEGNA has named veteran television executive Mellynda Hartel president and general manager of three Florida stations. She'll oversee First Coast News in Jacksonville and CBS affiliate WTSP in Tampa. Hartel brings more than 30 years of experience and most recently led FOX stations KTVU and KICU in San Francisco.
Stay current with more media news, the latest jobs and free industry tools at MediaJobsReport.com.
